pullRequest.title: fix(label): support label names containing spaces
pullRequest.body:
### Describe what this PR does / why we need it

`:Octo label remove "Needs Triage"` answered "Cannot find label: \"Needs". A user command splits its
arguments on whitespace, so the command received `"Needs` and `Triage"` and looked the label up by the
first word only. The same happened for `label add`, `label create`, `label delete` and `label edit`.

The label arguments are now joined back into one name, with a surrounding pair of quotes dropped, before
the label is looked up, so label names containing spaces work with and without quotes. A single word
label, and a call without a label, behave as before, picker fallback included.

### Does this pull request fix one issue?

Fixes #1141

### Describe how you did it

A local `join_args` helper in `lua/octo/commands.lua` packs the varargs, joins them with a space and strips
a surrounding `"..."` or `'...'` pair. It returns `nil` when nothing was passed, so `create_label`,
`label_action`, and the `edit` and `delete` handlers keep falling back to their prompt or picker exactly as
they did when the subcommands took a single argument. The five label subcommands now take varargs and pass
the joined name through.

### Describe how to verify it

The new spec `lua/tests/plenary/commands_label_spec.lua` stubs the label entry points and drives the command
dispatcher with the argument list a user command actually produces. With `nargs = "*"`,
`:Octo label remove "Needs Triage"` arrives as `{"label", "remove", '"Needs', 'Triage"'}`, which the spec
mirrors.

Without the fix 5 of its 7 cases fail (for example, expected `Needs Triage`, got `Needs`); with the fix all
7 pass.

Commands run on Windows 11 with Neovim v0.12.6:

```
nvim --headless --noplugin -u lua/tests/minimal_init.vim -c "lua require('plenary.busted').run('lua/tests/plenary/commands_label_spec.lua')"
```

All 24 spec files under `lua/tests/plenary/` pass with the change (0 failures, 0 errors), which is the same
set of files the `PlenaryBustedDirectory` CI job runs. `stylua --check` passes on the changed files, and
`lua-language-server` 3.18.2 with `--check lua/octo --checklevel=Information` reports no problems.

### Special notes for reviews

`doc/octo.txt` gained one example line for a label name with a space.

### Checklist

- [x] Passing tests and linting standards
- [x] Documentation updates in README.md and doc/octo.txt

AI was used to write this code.
